question.worked_solution:
First, we expand the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)^{2}+(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)^{2} & =({sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x-2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x)+({sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x+2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x) \\  & =({sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x-\cancel{2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x})+({sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x+\cancel{2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x}) \\  & ={sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x \\  & =2{sin}^{2}⁡x+2{cos}^{2}⁡x \\  & =2({sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use ${sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x=1$ to simplify the expression in the parentheses. This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}2({sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x)=2\cdot (1)=2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
(\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)^{2}+(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)^{2}=2.
$$
